intended_object: The canonical ring isomorphism κ(0) ≃ K between the residue field of an abelian variety A/K at its identity point and the ground field K, given by the evaluation map of the zero section (a K-rational point). Inferred from the docstring and name.
explanation: The body applies the library's general `residueFieldRingEquivOfSection` to the zero section, using `zeroSection_comp_toOver_hom` (zero section composed with the structure map is the identity of Spec K). The general construction turns Mathlib's evaluation map `X.descResidueField (Scheme.stalkClosedPointTo s)` into a ring isomorphism via `RingEquiv.ofBijective`. Mathematically this is the standard fact that a section through x makes K → κ(x) → K the identity, so κ(x) ≅ K. `zeroPoint` is defined as the zero section applied to the closed point of Spec K, so the stalk in the type is exactly the one the general construction expects. The map is the canonical evaluation map, matching the docstring. The general version, for any rational point of any K-scheme, already exists in the library, and this is only its specialization to the identity point of an abelian variety. A specific object is not too narrow merely for being specific. Mathlib has no declaration naming this isomorphism.
